headline: 7 dead, 1,593 hospitalized as dengue cases surge in Bangladesh
summary: Health officials report a worrying increase in infections and deaths, with September's first 15 days already seeing more deaths than all of August.
details: Seven people, including four women and three men, died from dengue in the last 24 hours, according to the Health Emergency Operation Center and Control Room of the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS).
In the same period, 1,593 new patients were admitted to hospitals across the country, with 1,004 men and 589 women among the newly infected.
The highest number of new admissions occurred in the Dhaka division (excluding city corporations), with 383 patients, followed by Khulna division with 290 patients.
Since January 1, 2024, a total of 55,163 people have been infected with dengue, and 164 people have died, according to DGHS data.
A concerning trend is emerging: while 43 people died in August, 67 people have already died in the first 15 days of September, indicating a sharp rise in fatalities.
Currently, 4,058 dengue patients remain hospitalized across various facilities in Bangladesh.
Among the city corporations, Dhaka South City Corporation has recorded the highest number of deaths, with 51 fatalities reported so far this year.

headline_marked: 2 killed in [[three-way collision between auto-rickshaw, car, and pickup]] in Chandpur
headline: 2 killed in three-way collision between auto-rickshaw, car, and pickup in Chandpur
summary: The accident occurred on the Chandpur-Cumilla regional highway on Tuesday afternoon, leaving two dead and two others injured.
details: A three-way collision involving a CNG-powered auto-rickshaw, a private car, and a pickup truck killed two people on the Chandpur-Cumilla regional highway.
The accident took place on Tuesday afternoon near Mahamaya in Chandpur Sadar upazila, in front of Mandari Kamal Mizi's house.
The deceased have been identified as Mohor Ali (60) from Fatehpur village in Kochua upazila and the auto-rickshaw driver, Kabir Mal.

Witnesses said a private car suddenly braked, causing the auto-rickshaw following behind to crash into it. The auto-rickshaw then lost control and collided with a pickup truck coming from the opposite direction.
The driver and passengers of the auto-rickshaw were thrown onto the road. Local residents rescued them and rushed them to the 250-bed Chandpur Sadar Hospital.
One victim was declared dead on arrival, while another died while being transported to Dhaka for advanced treatment.
Police from the Chandpur Sadar Model Police Station seized the three vehicles involved in the crash. The bodies have since been handed over to their families.
Local authorities, including former Union Parishad Chairman Swapon Mahmud, assisted in clearing the road to restore normal traffic flow.
